title: Azure Search (Part 2)
content:
In Part 1 I set up a full-text search in the Azure portal. In this part I search by meaning. I follow Microsoft's [Quickstart: Vector search in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-get-started-portal-import-vectors) and index six health-plan [PDF documents](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/azure-search-sample-data/tree/main/health-plan), so that I can ask a question in plain English and get back the passage that answers it.

Here is the plan. I create a resource group, an Azure OpenAI resource with an embedding model, and a storage account that holds the PDFs. I then create a search service, give it permission to reach the other two, and run the import data wizard.

:::brain-power Before you read on
A keyword search for deductible finds the word deductible. If I ask Which plan has the lowest deductible?, what would a search need to understand to find the right passage, even if the passage never uses my exact words?
:::

## Create a resource group

I put everything in one resource group, so that I can delete it all in one step when I have finished.

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.05.44-PM.png)
*I created a resource group called vectorsearch in East US, so that everything for this walkthrough lives in one place*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.05.59-PM.png)
*I reviewed the resource group settings and clicked Create*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.06.21-PM.png)

## Create the Azure OpenAI resource

The search service cannot turn text into vectors by itself. It borrows an embedding model from Azure OpenAI.

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.07.09-PM.png)
*I searched the Marketplace for openai and chose Azure OpenAI*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.11.55-PM.png)
*I named the Azure OpenAI resource vectorsearchopenai, put it in the vectorsearch resource group in East US, and chose the Standard S0 pricing tier*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.12.20-PM.png)
*I left the network setting on All networks, which is fine for a walkthrough*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.12.30-PM.png)
*I did not add any tags*

## Deploy an embedding model

The resource is only a container. To use a model, I have to deploy one.

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.15.02-PM.png)
*The Model deployments page is empty, so I used Deploy model, then Deploy base model*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.16.01-PM.png)
*I searched for text-embedding-ada-002, an embeddings model, and clicked Confirm*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.16.34-PM.png)
*I accepted the Standard deployment type and the default model version, and deployed the model*

:::no-dumb-questions
**Q: What is an embedding?**

A: A list of numbers that stands for the meaning of a piece of text. The text-embedding-ada-002 model turns each chunk of text into 1,536 numbers, and chunks with similar meanings get similar numbers. That is what lets a search match meaning and not just words.

**Q: Why not just search for the words?**

A: A keyword search misses a passage that says out-of-pocket maximum when I ask about the cost limit. A vector search can still find it, because the two phrases sit close together in meaning.
:::

## Get the documents into storage

The documents are six PDFs from Microsoft's sample data.

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.19.54-PM.png)
*The health-plan folder in the Azure-Samples repository holds the six PDF files I used as my documents*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.29.11-PM.png)
*I created a storage account called vectorsearchstorageac in the vectorsearch resource group, with Standard performance and locally redundant storage*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.29.58-PM.png)
*The storage account deployment is complete*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.30.34-PM.png)
*I created a private container called healthplan*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.31.24-PM.png)
*I uploaded the six PDF files into the healthplan container*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.31.56-PM.png)
*The healthplan container now lists all six PDF files as block blobs*

## Start on the permissions

The search service has to read the PDFs from the container. I started adding a role assignment on the container, and then I realised that I could not finish it until the search service existed.

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.32.15-PM.png)
*In the container's Access control (IAM), I started to add a role assignment*

![](assets/images/azuresearchvector/Screenshot-2026-02-09-at-5.33.08-PM.png)
*I chose the Storage Blob Data Reader role, which allows read access to blob containers and data. I stopped here, because the search service did not exist yet*
